thread:
Aria: Heads-up: release window tonight 02:00 UTC. Changes include cidr split for tenant-vpc, route propagation updates, and an IAM policy attach for edge-proxy. Need a concise canary + rollback plan.
Parker: I'll take the vpc canary. Suggest we test CIDR split in a shadow VPC (staging-shadow) first, then apply to staging-a, then prod. Keep IAM attach last.
Rohit: +1. Also we should enforce provider pin in the repo before apply. I spotted provider aws 4.5.2 in lockfile; ensure it's in the root `required_providers` block.
Parker: @DeployBot please run a preflight plan on branch release/cidr-split-2026 and provide a plan file.
DeployBot: Preflight started for commit sha: a9c4d2f. Running `terraform init -backend-config=... -upgrade=false`. Lockfile reports provider aws 4.5.2, module network v2.0.0 (pinned).
DeployBot: Plan result: 10 to add, 3 to change, 0 to destroy. Warning: changing `aws_vpc` cidr_block might require resource replacement. Manual approval required for replace ops.
Aria: Important: resource replacement for VPC will create a new VPC then reattach subnets 30 we need explicit migration steps and a traffic cutover plan.
Rohit: Let's avoid in-place replacement where possible. For the canary, we'll create the new VPC in parallel and route a shadow ENI to proxy traffic. If smoke is green, migrate routes and update LB.
Parker: Rollback plan if canary fails: 1) revert git to a9c4d2f~1, 2) import previous state snapshot to staging (`terraform state push` with backed-up file), 3) re-route traffic back to original ENI, 4) verify connectivity. I'll document commands in the runbook.
DevOpsBot: Snapshot created: s3://redwood-ops/tf-backups/cidr-split-2026-staging.json (etag: "abc123etag"). Recommend keeping this for 72h.
Aria: Add a safety mutex in release notes: "No IAM policy detach or role replacement during CIDR migration wave." We block parallel IAM detach in CI with a lint rule for this window.
DeployBot: No drift detected. Plan file stored at /tmp/plan-a9c4d2f.out. ETA window: 02:00-02:30 UTC. Apply queued.
Rohit: Apply snippet I'll run for shadow canary:
```
export TF_VAR_region=us-east-1
git checkout a9c4d2f
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-tfstate" -upgrade=false
terraform plan -out=plan-shadow.out -var-file=release/cidr.tfvars -target=module.network["staging-shadow"]
terraform apply plan-shadow.out
```
Parker: After apply I'll run these checks: BGP sessions up, route table propagation, sample tenant connectivity (curl /health), and confirm IAM policy count unchanged. Post `SHADOW OK` or `SHADOW FAIL` with timestamps.
Aria: Oncall, can you mute paging 02:00-02:30 and have infra-sre on standby? Tag: @oncall-bot
oncall-bot: acknowledged. Pager muted for window. escalation: infra-sre if `CANARY FAIL`.
Rohit: If we need to rollback quickly, we use the snapshot restore flow:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ops/tf-backups/cidr-split-2026-staging.json ./state-restore.json
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-tfstate"
terraform state push state-restore.json
git revert a9c4d2f
terraform apply -auto-approve -var-file=release/cidr.tfvars
```
Parker: Note: avoid `-target` destroy. Our rollback prefers restoring prior full state + reapply.
Aria: If shadow OK at 02:10, proceed to staging-a with a stagger: apply AZ1, wait 3m, apply AZ2, then run IAM attach wave. If any unexpected role detaches appear, abort and revert.
DeployBot: Scheduled apply queued at 02:00 UTC for shadow canary. Webhook: https://deploybot.internal/redwood/ops/queues/1723300000
Parker: I'll also add a temporary alert rule to Prometheus for `route53_latency > 500ms` and `lb_5xx_rate > 0.5%` for 10m. If triggered, we'll mark `CANARY FAIL`.
Aria: Good. I'll draft the release notes with the rollback checklist and module pins. Keep messages short in this chan during window: `SHADOW START`, `SHADOW OK/FAIL`, `STAGING START`, `STAGING OK/FAIL`, `PROD START/COMPLETE`.
Rohit: One last thing 3 confirm terraform workspace is correct for staging. CI check added to ensure `terraform workspace show` matches expected.
Parker: Thanks all. Ping me in thread if you see `aws_vpc` replacement planned during apply. I'll be watching the logs and will cut traffic if needed. :shield:
